name: Logseq
tagline: Source-available, local-first outliner with bidirectional linking
painPoints: Outliner format is polarizing — not everyone thinks in bullet hierarchies
Performance degrades significantly with large graphs
Sync is limited and the mobile experience is unreliable
No proactive AI or automation for capturing information automatically
Requires manual maintenance to keep the graph useful
metaDescription: Looking for a Logseq alternative? GAIA is source-available AI that triages email, manages tasks, and runs workflows across your tools. Self-hostable.
whyPeopleLook: Logseq's source-available, local-first approach to networked thought has attracted users who want privacy and data ownership alongside bidirectional linking. But like Obsidian, Logseq demands constant manual input. Every note, link, and tag is your responsibility. Performance issues with large graphs and a buggy mobile experience have driven many users to seek alternatives — particularly ones that combine knowledge management with proactive AI assistance.
gaiaReplaces: Automatic knowledge graph construction from email and calendar data
Semantic search over personal knowledge without manual tagging
Meeting note capture without manual journaling
Context surfacing during tasks without searching your graph manually
gaiaAdvantages: Knowledge is captured automatically without manual journal entries
Consistent mobile and sync experience across all platforms
Proactive intelligence surfaces relevant knowledge without searching
Email and calendar context enriches the knowledge graph automatically
migrationSteps: Export your Logseq database as Markdown or JSON
Import key notes into GAIA's memory for semantic retrieval
Connect Gmail and Google Calendar to automatically enrich GAIA's memory
Use GAIA's query interface to retrieve knowledge instead of manual graph navigation

faqs.question: Does GAIA support Markdown like Logseq?
faqs.answer: GAIA can read and process Markdown files from your Logseq export. It does not provide a Logseq-style outliner interface but can answer questions and surface information from ingested Markdown notes.

faqs.question: Is GAIA source-available like Logseq?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both GAIA and Logseq are source-available (PolyForm Noncommercial). GAIA's GitHub repository is publicly available and accepts community contributions.

faqs.question: Does GAIA have better mobile support than Logseq?
faqs.answer: GAIA works on phones through the web app and chat bots, sidestepping the sync and performance issues Logseq's mobile client has historically had.

faqs.question: Can GAIA replace Logseq for daily journaling?
faqs.answer: GAIA can capture daily context automatically from your email and calendar, but it does not provide a journaling interface for free-form writing. If daily journaling is central to your workflow, Logseq or Obsidian may still be valuable alongside GAIA.

comparisonRows.gaia: Knowledge graph that builds itself from email and calendar, instead of manual capture and linking
comparisonRows.competitor: Local-first outliner and PKM for manually capturing, linking, and navigating personal knowledge via a bidirectional graph

comparisonRows.gaia: Connections inferred by AI across people, projects, and conversations, with no outliner discipline required
comparisonRows.competitor: Block-based outliner with bidirectional page and block references, daily journal pages, and a visual knowledge graph for navigating connections

comparisonRows.gaia: Emails monitored and triaged automatically, enriching the graph with no copying into pages
comparisonRows.competitor: No email integration. Emails must be manually copied or summarized into Logseq pages; no inbox monitoring or automated triage

comparisonRows.gaia: Tasks captured from email and calendar with AI prioritization and deadline reminders, beyond markers and queries
comparisonRows.competitor: TODO/DONE markers and query blocks within the outliner allow basic task tracking; no AI prioritization, deadline reminders, or cross-tool task capture

comparisonRows.gaia: Calendar events created and managed with meeting context, not read-only views through plugins
comparisonRows.competitor: No native calendar integration. Community plugins offer limited read-only calendar views, but no event creation or scheduling actions

comparisonRows.gaia: Proactive automation and cross-tool AI actions built in, not experimental blocks you invoke by hand
comparisonRows.competitor: AI features are experimental and community-driven via plugins (e.g., GPT-4 prompting blocks); no proactive automation or cross-tool AI actions built in

comparisonRows.gaia: Actions triggered in external tools from knowledge, beyond filtering notes dynamically
comparisonRows.competitor: No workflow automation engine. Advanced queries can filter and display notes dynamically, but cannot trigger actions in external tools

comparisonRows.gaia: Native connections to email, calendar, and project tools, not a file system plus community plugins
comparisonRows.competitor: Community plugin ecosystem for limited integrations; primarily file-system based with no native connections to email, calendar, or project management services

comparisonRows.gaia: Source-available and self-hostable like Logseq, with consistent sync across all platforms
comparisonRows.competitor: Open-source client with local-first file storage (Markdown and EDN); the upcoming Logseq DB version introduces a proprietary sync layer

comparisonRows.gaia: Hosted: paid plan at ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month; self-hosting free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs)
comparisonRows.competitor: Free and open source for the desktop app; sync and collaboration features in the upcoming DB version are expected to carry a subscription cost
